dates.description: Launch date of Apollo 11 from Kennedy Space Center at 13:32:00 UTC
Landing/splashdown date of Apollo 11 in the Pacific Ocean at 16:50:35 UTC
Epoch of orbital parameters; also date Apollo 11 entered lunar orbit at 17:21:50 UTC
Orbital departure from lunar orbit at 04:55:42 UTC
Lunar landing date of Eagle at 20:17:40 UTC and moonwalk
Return launch of Eagle from the Moon at 17:54:00 UTC; also docking with ascent stage and Luna 15 crash date
Docking with Lunar module date at 16:56:03 UTC
Undocking date with Lunar module at 17:44:00 UTC
Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the first artificial satellite
Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space
Alan Shepard became the first American in space
Kennedy addressed Congress on 'Urgent National Needs' declaring goal to land a man on the Moon
Kennedy delivered his 'We choose to go to the Moon' speech at Rice University
Kennedy met with Khrushchev and proposed a joint Moon project
Kennedy again proposed a joint Moon expedition in a speech to the UN General Assembly
NASA head James Webb announced lunar orbit rendezvous would be used
Apollo 1 launchpad fire killed Grissom, White, and Chaffee
Apollo 7 evaluated the command module in Earth orbit
Apollo 8 tested the command module in lunar orbit
Apollo 9 tested the lunar module in Earth orbit
Apollo 10 conducted a dress rehearsal in lunar orbit
Soviet Union launched Luna 15 probe
Release of Luna 15 transmission recordings for 40th anniversary of Apollo 11
Initial crew assignment of Armstrong, Lovell, and Aldrin as backup crew for Apollo 9 officially announced
STS-26 mission, next after Apollo 11 with all-experienced crew
Anders accepted job with National Aeronautics and Space Council effective August 1969
NASA's Apollo Site Selection Board announced five potential landing sites
Apollo 10's lunar module flew within 15 km of Site 2
Press conference announcing Armstrong would be first to walk on the Moon
Ascent stage of LM-5 Eagle arrived at Kennedy Space Center
CSM-107 Columbia arrived at Kennedy Space Center
CSM was mated
CSM moved from Operations and Checkout Building to Vehicle Assembly Building
S-IVB third stage of Saturn V arrived
S-II second stage arrived
S-IC first stage arrived
Saturn V Instrument Unit arrived
Saturn V assembly departed Vehicle Assembly Building for Launch Pad 39A
Countdown test commenced
Countdown test concluded
Launch complex floodlit; mobile service structure carried back to parking area
Publication of Jules Verne's novel 'From the Earth to the Moon' referencing the Columbiad cannon
Eisenhower dollar coin released using the eagle from the Apollo 11 patch design
Susan B. Anthony dollar unveiled using the same eagle design
Collins' book published referencing Columbia name origin
Chris Kraft's autobiography revealed meeting about first-step decision
Don Eyles' Guidance and Control Conference paper on program alarms
Armstrong interview explaining time and distance limits on first moonwalk
